earlier.v: 1 PASSED its final test: the climax reversal (a fall of 3+ hourly standard deviations on 3x+ volume that closes in the top 40% of the hour; buy, hold 12 hours): +5.3% a year over the market, z 2.35 against 2.33 on 324 untouched coins (+7.4%, z 2.54 on 140; +2.5%, z 2.30 on 25); on paper from 19 Oct 2026. The rest failed the screen or did not beat the plain setup. Described: dips with heavy aggressive selling did worse over the next day (-0.25%); a dip on one coin alone did better than a market-wide one (+0.55%, not significant).

earlier.name: What moves the market (descriptive, 165 coins, hourly 2020-2026): what explains an hourly move, whether flow predicts, when moves happen, CPI and FOMC hours, options expiry, the CME weekend, what follows big moves, and the climax rule’s anatomy
earlier.v: the market explains ~60% of a coin’s hourly move, its own aggressive flow ~6% more; this hour’s movers and most-bought coins give a little back next hour (too small after fees); busiest 13-16 UTC and 00 UTC, quietest 03-11 UTC and weekends; CPI hour 1.3x and FOMC hour 1.9x a normal hour (FOMC hours rose 2021-24, not 2025-26); no options-expiry effect; no CME gap fill; after 3-sigma market falls the market rebounded +0.8% in 24h; the climax rule rides that rebound; rejected 3-sigma spikes lagged the market for 3 days (hypothesis)

lessons: Rules that predict direction look good where they are found and fade or reverse on new coins (rounds 5–12).
Being paid for supplying leverage works: the funding harvest (spot + short perpetual) passed untouched tests in rounds 7, 8, 10 and, paired with RSI(5) dip-buying, in round 12.

The harvest pays mostly in boom years (2021, 2024); funding thinned in 2025–26 (BTC’s own funding about 12% a year in 2024, 5% in 2025, 2% so far in 2026), and the 10-coin harvest made about 0% on 140 coins in those two years.
Close a pair when its perpetual is delisted; a coin’s funding can turn violently negative in a squeeze (DEXE, July 2026: −77% in a week, charged hourly).
Per-coin strategy picks do not persist (40% against 50% for chance, round 9).
Carry across coins earns a lot in some years and falls 50–80% when crowded coins rally.
The basis (perpetual vs spot) costs about 0.05% a year on large coins.
Forex carry and trend did not pay in 2009–2026.
Trend-following was positive on every coin set (+5 to +15% a year over the market) but never clear of chance, with 15–25% falls.

Buying 5-sigma hourly falls with the perpetual at a discount paid on 165 seen coins and failed on 324 untouched ones (round 14): direction rules keep fading on new coins. Shorting 5-sigma rises lost everywhere.
CREED’s replayed profit came from hindsight in when setups were shown: taken when shown it has no edge, and no exit change creates one.

The first direction rule to pass all three stages (round 16) reads a footprint: a selling climax that buyers take back within the same hour. A big fall alone, or with volume, sellers or a discount (round 14), was not enough; the buying inside the hour was.

About 60% of an altcoin’s hourly move is the whole market (round 17); scheduled US data (CPI, FOMC) are the biggest planned moves; folklore like the CME gap fill and options-expiry pinning did not show up.

When a backtest looks great on one set of coins, it usually means that set (round 18: an order-flow rule made +47% a year on new listings and nothing on 165 older coins). Funding income in 2025–26 sat in new listings without a spot market to hedge with.
